title: Structured logging: SLF4J as the facade, Logback, Log4j2 and TinyLog

videos.script: An order fails at three in the morning. The only witness is the log. {{log}} If the log says nothing useful, nobody finds out what happened. This lesson makes the bookshop's log worth reading. {{facade}} First, the two halves of logging in Java. Your code talks to SLF4J, a facade. Behind it sits one backend that writes the lines, and in Spring Boot that is Logback. {{levels}} Then levels and logger names, and why a message is written with placeholders instead of joined strings. {{requestid}} Then one id per request. A filter puts it on every line the request causes, and hands it back to the client in a header. When somebody reports a failure, that id finds every line of it. {{json}} Then the same lines as JSON, one object per line, ready for a log platform to search by field. {{backends}} Last, the other backends, Log4j2 and TinyLog, and the vulnerability that showed what a logging library can do when it reads too much into a message. And all the way through, the things a log must never hold. {{never}}
